analytical_findings: For completed nongrazing identical-particle central-potential encounters in a uniform field, the branch-dependent transverse reflection combined with time reversal leaves qB unchanged and defines an involution modulo axial rotation.

The reciprocal map preserves Gibbs-weighted incoming crossing flux; its reduced absolute Jacobian is b*u*p/(b_star*u_star*p_star). The removed impact angle has absolute Jacobian one, including its anti-equivariant sign.

On the completed reciprocal core C=D intersect R(D), the exact conditional mean magnetic-moment increment integrates to zero. Adding constructed reverse partners to enforce numerical cancellation was not used.
The bounded band contains a small flux subset whose inverse is outside the band. Its large contribution to the signed drift prevents interpreting that drift as full-equilibrium plasma cooling.
Two close encounters miss endpoint accuracy although energy and moment checks pass; conserved moments alone do not certify a trajectory.
novelty_scope: A tested model-specific reciprocity benchmark and finite-box diagnostic. No priority claim for reciprocity, magnetic-moment exchange or variance reduction. JB20 arXiv:2008.06080v1 printed p.6 Eq.(20) and following discussion distinguishes ordinary time reversal in an external magnetic field from general postulated detailed balance; printed p.3 Eqs.(1)-(2) motivates equilibrium correlations and potential of mean force.
